pr_title: Add basic error handling and logging to Volumio

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.

Issue https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/42823 mentioned that the Volumio integration was not handling errors well in case of no response from the Volumio API. This PR aims to wrap all the calls to the api with proper error handling.

TO DO: the Volumio integration does not seem to fail very gracefully in case of lost connection. The media_player entity will remain available and the logs will fill with warnings about the state update. This could be improved but is not yet in this PR.

Hey there @onfreund, mind taking a look at this pull request as its been labeled with an integration (`volumio`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L493) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

Thanks @wouterbaake 

I think a better approach would be to start with a coordinator. It will take care of the logs, and mark the entity as not available, which should also handle service calls (with the exception of service calls before the entity is marked unavailable).

> Thanks @wouterbaake
> 
> I think a better approach would be to start with a coordinator. It will take care of the logs, and mark the entity as not available, which should also handle service calls (with the exception of service calls before the entity is marked unavailable).

Well, I think each service call would still need error handling because pyvolumio throws an exception on timeout. So if you do not catch those you will fill the logs with unhandled exceptions.

Will you approve this PR? I think it makes an improvement and can be a starting point for the next step of using a coordinator.

> Well, I think each service call would still need error handling because pyvolumio throws an exception on timeout. So if you do not catch those you will fill the logs with unhandled exceptions.

From a purist perspective, yes, but if the entity is marked as unavailable, HA will block those service calls anyway, so this is only dealing with the edge case of "entity has not yet been marked unavailable yet a service was called".
I'd really rather start with the updater.

Hey there @onfreund, mind taking a look at this issue as its been labeled with an integration (`volumio`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L493) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>
Not sure what you mean by "check before attempting to connect". The integration is failing to connect, and thus prints out an error.

Hi - thanks for looking into this.

I guess I'm comparing with the Roku errors in the same log above - both the Roku & Volumio are powered off, Roku fails gracefully, Volumio causes a cascade of errors.

It's been a while since I've done any serious programming, but I had a look at the pyvolumio code on github, and I'm not sure if it's that's the problem, or the home-assistant media_player code?

So, in my imagination, HA & the Volumio integration would try a simple network test first (ie perhaps open a network socket first?) and then catch that with a generic "volumio's not there" response. If that test passed, then the call to get_state would be more likely to succeed.

Does that make sense? :) 

The problem is that this is just a noisy failure, filling the HA logs and makes it difficult to look at a completely different and unrelated issue.
I am working on adding some error handling to the Volumio integration for each call to the API, borrowing from Roku's implementation.

More than happy to review a PR with better error handling.
However, I do think there needs to be at least one log when failing to connect (it doesn't have to repeat every 60 seconds though), so if the objective is to have zero logs, my recommendation would be to change the log level for the integration in your deployment.

Sounds ideal!
I agree that _something_ needs to be logged on initial failure to connect - from HA's point of view, a loss of connection has to be handled anyway to report to the end user that Volumio's not controllable, then, when Volumio responds the logging can resume...
But, a common network connection catch for a known good / fail condition might be all that's needed? I presume every API call would need to catch a network failure scenario? (I've not looked at the Roku code)
Anyway, more importantly, thanks for looking into this.
